groups.title: THE FIRST YEARS ARE NOT LITTLE YEARS.
groups.description: Before children can explain who they are, they are already showing us. In the questions they ask.

drawer.title: THE FIRST YEARS ARE NOT LITTLE YEARS.
paragraphs: Before children can explain who they are, they are already showing us.
In the questions they ask.
The stories they love.
The things they build again and again.
The way they make friends.
The way they move.
The things that make them laugh.
The moments they hesitate.
And the moments they suddenly say:
"I can do it!"
At My School ITALY, we believe early education begins by noticing these moments.
Because before we teach a child, we should first try to understand them

drawer.title: WHAT IF A PRESCHOOL COULD NOTICE MORE?
paragraphs: Not only what your child knows.
But...
What makes them curious?
How they approach something new.

This is where the MSI experience becomes different.
WE DON'T JUST TEACH THE CHILD.
WE LEARN FROM THE CHILD TOO.

drawer.title: STORIES ARE WHERE OUR CLASSROOMS COME ALIVE
paragraphs: Once Upon a Time Can Lead Almost Anywhere.
At My School ITALY, stories are not something we save for the end of the lesson.
Stories can become the lesson.
A curious character can lead children towards a new word.
A journey can introduce numbers.
An animal can open a conversation about science.
A river can lead to geography.
A disappearing species can begin a conversation about protecting our planet.
And one little question in a story can keep a classroom thinking for the rest of the day.
LISTEN → WATCH → CONNECT → PRACTISE → MOVE & CREATE → PERFORM
English. Mathematics. Science. Understanding the World. Creativity. Values.
All connected through experiences children can remember

drawer.title: SMALL TUMMIES. BIG DEVELOPMENTAL NEEDS.
paragraphs: INSPIRE ME EAT
Breakfast. Lunch. Snacks.
Mealtimes are about more than food.
Children learn to hold, pour, choose, communicate, wait, share, taste and gradually become more independent.
Nutrition, age-appropriate textures, portions, hygiene and positive mealtime experiences are part of the MSI day.
Because even a spoon can become a learning tool
